svg.title: Where duplicate Meta purchases come from
svg.desc: Troubleshooting map. Start with one test order and count how many Purchase events reached Meta. If the browser and server IDs differ, share one event_id. If the names differ, use the same event name. If two integrations both send Purchase, pick one owner. If the Pixel fires again on a page reload, fire once per order. If the server retries with new IDs, keep the order ID on retries. If everything matches, compare over a longer period because attribution differences are normal.
svg.text: Meta purchases higher than your orders? Check these in order
Place one test order, then walk down the list. Stop at the first "yes".
Start: one test order (e.g. ORDER-1042). How many Purchase events reached Meta for it?

g.text: 1. Do the browser eventID and server event_id differ?
Usually random IDs generated separately on each side.
A platform app plus a plugin, or an old CAPI tool still active.
4. Does the Pixel fire again when the thank-you page reloads?
Browser-only repeats aren't something to rely on Meta to clean up.
5. Do server retries get a new ID?
A queue or webhook retry that builds a fresh event_id.

svg.text: All clear? Then the gap is probably attribution (view-through, windows, dates), not duplicates. Compare 2–4 weeks.
Based on Meta's deduplication rules. Order ID is an example.
